decision.summary: Landlord asked us to enter today and change locks over suspected Airbnb subletting. We refused as there was no 24h notice and no emergency. We replied to the landlord, gave the tenant proper notice for Monday, and escalated the subletting concern to legal.

answers.question: Can the agency enter the property today?
answers.answer: No. Clause 7.1 and the law require 24h written notice, and a suspected sublet is not an emergency. Holding a key gives no right of entry. Changing locks on an occupying tenant risks unlawful eviction.

answers.question: What do you reply to the landlord?
answers.answer: A polite refusal that explains why, says notice has been given for Monday 12 Oct 10-12, asks for evidence, and asks her not to act herself (MSG-101).

answers.question: What do you do about the subletting suspicion?
answers.answer: Treat it as an unproven allegation. Gather evidence through a noticed inspection and escalate to legal (ESC-103). Tenant was not told of the allegation. No lock change.

assumptions: Monday 10:00-12:00 is a reasonable time and more than 24h away
Tenant is vulnerable, so contact is by email only

args.body:
Dear Margaret,

Thank you for letting us know. I'm sorry, but we can't enter 27 Bethnal Green Road today or change the locks. Jonah has the right to live there undisturbed. The tenancy (clause 7.1) needs at least 24 hours' written notice for an inspection, and holding a spare key doesn't give us the right to enter. Changing locks on a tenant who is living there could be unlawful eviction, which is a criminal offence for you and for us. A suspicion of subletting isn't an emergency that would allow entry.

What we're doing: we've sent Jonah written notice of a routine inspection on Monday 12 October, 10:00-12:00. We'll take photos of the condition of the flat and note who is there. We've also passed the subletting concern to our legal team. Clause 9.3 does forbid subletting without your written consent, but any action has to follow the proper legal process, and we'll advise you on that.

It would help if you could send the neighbour's description and dates of what she saw, and any Airbnb listing link you have. Please don't take any action yourself, such as changing locks or removing belongings.

Kind regards,
Mare & Co Lettings
